artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: five hardening changes to scripts/move-modules.py with red-before/green-after fixture tests, the pre-move replay result (17 provenance READMEs + 2 ADRs + SYNC-MAP skipped), the relocation playbook, and the harness caveat (INV red in the shared tree from a sibling's uncommitted edits).

completion_data.completion_summary: Hardened scripts/move-modules.py with --no-rewrite (three built-in defaults), an identical-sides warning with --strict, an ambiguous-stem refusal, a namespace-declaration refusal with --namespace-paths, and a moved-versus-rewritten report line with a zero-move non-zero exit; added the 28-test stdlib fixture harness scripts/test-move-modules.py including a history-gated replay that reports exactly the Expressiveness extraction's 17 provenance READMEs as skipped; and wrote docs/development/MODULE_RELOCATION.md. check-module-invariants.sh --no-build is red on INV only in the shared tree, caused by a concurrent sibling's uncommitted FormalSystem .lean edits; INV passes on an isolated export of HEAD plus this task's files.

memory_candidates.content: When a whole-repo gate harness is red in a working tree shared with concurrent agents, attribute the redness mechanically instead of arguing it: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $SCRATCH`, copy only your own working files over, `git init` + commit in the scratch copy, and run the gate there. Checks that depend on untracked build output (e.g. a warning budget reading .lake traces) will fail in the export for environmental reasons, so read the two runs together: a check is cleared if it passes in whichever environment it is measurable in.

Testing a hyphen-named, run-from-repo-root Python CLI in process: load it with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location (resolve the absolute path from __file__ before any chdir), build a disposable `git init` repo in tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, chdir in under try/finally, call the tool's run(argparse.Namespace(...)) under contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr, and translate SystemExit into a return code. Keep every flag default in one run_tool helper and read new flags in the tool with getattr(args, name, default) so older caller-built Namespaces keep working. A historical replay can be tested the same way against `git archive <commit>` plus an empty .git directory, gated by unittest.skipUnless(git cat-file -e).
